links.passage: The beneﬁt of using a high fertigation frequency on the crop yield was also conﬁrmed by a recent ﬁeld experiment using mulched drip irrigated maize in a semi-humid region of north-eastern China (Liu et al., 2015).
reference_entries: Liu Y, Li J, Li Y. 2015. Effects of split fertigation rates on the dynamics of nitrate in soil and the yield of mulched drip-irrigated maize in the sub-humid region. Applied Engineering in Agriculture 31(1): 103–117.

links.passage: Drip irrigation has several advantages over surface and sprinkler irrigation when applying wastewater to agricultural land because it can minimize the hazards of the microbial contamination of the air, soil and plants (Ayers and Westcot, 1994).
reference_entries: Ayers RS, Westcot DW. 1994. Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29, Rev. 1. Rome, Italy.

links.passage: The results showed that subsurface drip irrigation could prevent pathogen contamination.
supporting_passages: Moreover, the potential of using water containing moderate levels of E. coli for both surface and subsurface drip-irrigated asparagus lettuce was evaluated in a greenhouse over two seasons with three irrigation intervals (4, 8 and 12 days) and three pan coefﬁcients of 0.6, 0.8 and 1.0 (Li and Wen, 2016).
These results indicated that subsurface drip irrigation is a promising method for avoiding E. coli contamination when applying sewage efﬂuent.
links.inference_note: The preceding sentence carries the citation (Li and Wen, 2016) for the study whose results show subsurface drip prevents pathogen (E. coli) contamination of soil and plants when sewage effluent is applied.
reference_entries: Li J, Wen J. 2016. Effects of water managements on transport of E. coli in soil–plant system for drip irrigation applying secondary sewage efﬂuent. Agricultural Water Management 17: 12–20.

notes: Paper is a self-review of the author's lab research; sprinkler, VRI centre-pivot and uniformity-design findings fall outside the six technologies and were not reported; soil sensors only named as measurement tools.
